findings.title: The new payroll_completeness_question affordance has no by-name resolution case in needs-you-affordances.test.ts
findings.rule: apps/web/lib/firm/needs-you.ts's own extension-point note (read at lines ~150-156 of the current file): a new row kind's five sync points are '(4) components/firm/needs-you-affordances.tsx's NEEDS_YOU_AFFORDANCES registry + needs-you-affordances.test.ts's by-name resolution cases, (5) messages/en.json's NeedsYou.rowKind.* label map.' SWEEP-PLAN.md's own lane-04 section cites this same note as the standard ('A new row kind has five sync points, named in the file's own extension note').
findings.evidence: d0c2f6965 adds `payroll_completeness_question: PayrollCompletenessQuestionAffordance` to NEEDS_YOU_AFFORDANCES (needs-you-affordances.tsx) and does the en.json label (sync points 4a and 5), but `git diff 7bc5a710f...HEAD -- apps/web/components/firm/needs-you-affordances.test.ts` is empty, and `grep -n payroll_completeness_question apps/web/components/firm/needs-you-affordances.test.ts` returns no hits. That test file's own running commentary calls this the 'F8 discipline' — 'prove a real entry BY NAME rather than being inferred from the others still passing' — for exactly the case of a new non-null registry entry, which this is (it is not a `null`/no-inline-act kind like payroll_posting_blocked or rent_payable_unsettled).
findings.verified: Confirmed the gap is real (test file diff is empty, no case exists) and confirmed the mitigating context: the SAME sync point was already skipped for two prior non-null registrations, work_question (#629, 0180) and accrual_bill_conflict (#938), neither of which has a by-name case in this file either (grepped both names, zero hits). So this is a documented standard the file's own header still asserts as current practice, but one that has drifted out of actual observance for at least two tickets before this one — not a regression this ticket introduced alone, but also not corrected by it.
findings.required_fix: Add one case to needs-you-affordances.test.ts, in the file's own established shape: `test("getNeedsYouAffordance resolves payroll_completeness_question (#1048)", () => { assert.equal(typeof getNeedsYouAffordance("payroll_completeness_question"), "function"); });`. summary: Standards axis: high-quality, disciplined work across all four tickets, independently re-verified rather than taken on the reports' word — four prosrc sha256 pins, the registry version/count triple, the applied-migration checksums, and the new table's FORCE RLS/grant posture were all re-measured live on clara_l07 and matched; three test files were re-run independently (13+44+33 = 90 tests, all green, matching the reports' own counts) rather than trusted. Migration house law (prestate/tail pins, owner/SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/ACL preservation on every recut body, FORCE RLS with zero application-role DML on the one new relation, redo safety, immutable-migration recut convention) is followed correctly on both 0342 and 0343. TDD vertical-slice discipline holds throughout — no commit batches red tests ahead of implementation, and the one test-only commit per ticket (#1059's DB proof, #1048's final coverage cells) corresponds to the ticket's own stated 'no migration needed' premise or to additional coverage on an already-green slice, not to horizontal slicing. Shared files (tree.ts, needs-you.ts, manifest.txt, $GATES, CONTEXT.md, rig-meta.mjs, en.json) are all touched minimally and correctly per SWEEP-PLAN's own rules. One minor finding: the new payroll_completeness_question affordance was registered in needs-you-affordances.tsx and en.json but never given the by-name resolution case in needs-you-affordances.test.ts that needs-you.ts's own five-sync-point note calls for — a real, citable gap against a documented standard, though mitigated by the fact that the same sync point was already unobserved for two prior non-null row-kind additions (work_question, accrual_bill_conflict), so this ticket did not originate the drift.
